claims.text: A hybrid of machine-learned interatomic potentials and enhanced sampling can substantially reduce the cost of calculating fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The hybrid approach can retain fidelity to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
Machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on ab initio data can replace explicit ab initio molecular dynamics in phase free-energy calculations.
Enhanced sampling can efficiently explore the phase space needed for these free-energy calculations.
The proposed method is applicable when high-quality ab initio training data are available.
An MLIP can act as a surrogate for the ab initio potential-energy surface.
Using the surrogate potential enables efficient phase-space exploration and free-energy calculation.
MLIPs reduce computational cost by orders of magnitude relative to ab initio molecular dynamics.
Enhanced sampling ensures accurate exploration of the relevant phase-space regions.
The proposed method captures vibrational entropy and anharmonicity.
The proposed method captures electron–vibration coupling effects.
The hybrid approach will be at least ten times faster than explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
For elemental and binary systems, free energies and derived thermodynamic properties will agree with ab initio results within 5% error.
For multicomponent systems, free energies and derived thermodynamic properties will agree with ab initio results within 10% error.
The approach is valid for systems containing up to five principal components.
The approach is valid at temperatures up to 1.5 times the fusion temperature.
Accuracy depends on the quality of the MLIP training data.
Accuracy depends on whether enhanced sampling captures rare events and phase transitions.
